questions.prompt: What basic claim does Chapter 16 make about politics?
choices: It is only about rational policy optimization
It can pursue policy goals while also expressing group loyalty
It never concerns outcomes at all

explanation.gentle: The chapter widens politics beyond pure policy reasoning.
explanation.direct: Its main move is to treat participation as outcome pursuit plus visible group allegiance.
explanation.competitive: Politics can chase policy and signal the side together.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter treat democratic participation as group loyalty as well as policy reasoning?
choices: Because political acts can make side-taking and coalition identity publicly visible
Because policy never matters in public life
Because loyalty only exists in private and never in civic behavior

explanation.gentle: The chapter says participation can show where someone stands socially.
explanation.direct: Political action can function as readable allegiance, not only as issue selection.
explanation.competitive: The act can mark the jersey, not just the platform.

questions.prompt: Why do strong emotions and low information fit the chapter's model of politics?
choices: Because intense side-taking can persist even when detailed issue knowledge is thin
Because emotions automatically produce better policy analysis
Because information has no role in politics at all

explanation.gentle: The chapter says loyalty display can stay strong even when detail is sparse.
explanation.direct: Emotion and low information make more sense once politics is read partly as identity display.
explanation.competitive: The signal can stay hot even without full file depth.

Because loyalty disappears whenever outcomes matter
Because politics is only tribal theater

explanation.gentle: The chapter's hardest lesson is coexistence, not replacement.

explanation.competitive: Outcome concern and side signal can stack.
